land.text: the Black Sea coast and the Danube delta lands of the Second Bulgarian Empire from the Danube mouths to Varna and Emona; the Despotate of Dobruja page: 'The principality was spun off from the Second Bulgarian Empire'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws the Despotate from 1363; the Bulgarian dossier (eu-18-c) records the split in 1356.

land.text: most of the Dobrujan forts after the expedition of Candarli Ali Pasha in 1388 and Varna in 1389

successors.note: Dobruja page: the 1388 expedition 'brought most of the Dobrujan forts under Turkish rule'; Despotate page: 'Varna fell to the Ottomans' in 1389.

land.text: Dristra (Silistra) and the Danube side, which 'came under the control of Mircea the Elder' in 1388/1389

successors.note: The Ottomans recaptured the southern part in 1393 and again in 1397; Wallachia held Dobruja in 1404-1420 (Dobruja page).

capitals.name: Kaliakra
capitals.note: Infobox capital is Karvuna (Balchik, 43.41 N 28.16 E), the first seat, undated and tagged 'citation needed'; the page says the capital moved to Kaliakra under Dobrotitsa without a year. Schiltberger: 'Its capital is called Kaliakra' (Dobruja page).

capitals.name: Varna
capitals.note: 1386: Ivanko 'moved the capital from Kaliakra to Varna'; Varna fell in 1389.

correction.text: the 1363 shape (Dobruja between the Danube mouths and Varna/Emona) extended back to the 1356 split; the Dobruja page: in 1357 Dobrotitsa 'was mentioned as a despot ruling over a large territory, including the fortresses of Varna'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria begins in 1363 but the page gives 'existed from 1356 to 1411' (infobox 'Established: 1340s' under Balik). The page gives no boundary; the 1363 outline is used as the nearest drawn extent (confidence 2).

21,689 km2 for Dobruja between the Danube mouths and the Black Sea coast south to Emona. The Dobruja page has Varna held in 1357, Pangalia and other right-bank cities recognising Dobrotitsa in 1368. No infobox area on either page, so no area comparison is possible.

21,570 km2: the one added cell on the Burgas coast (about 27.65 E, 42.69 N, Nessebar) matches the Dobruja page's 'after 1369 ... some of the forts lost by the Bulgarians (Anchialos and Mesembria)'; the ledger carries it at confidence 1.

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid 1385-1387; from 1388 the ledger's losses (most forts to the Ottomans in 1388, Dristra to Wallachia in 1388/1389, Varna in 1389) take the land and the state ends in 1389

keyframe_review.note: Years only: Cliopatria keeps the Despotate whole to 1394. The Dobruja page: Ivanko killed in 1388, 'The expedition brought most of the Dobrujan forts under Turkish rule'; the Despotate page: Varna fell in 1389. 1390-1394 belong to the Ottoman and Wallachian holders (Bayezid took 'the southern part of the territory in 1393', Dobruja page). Same extent otherwise (21,570 km2).

region.text: the region of modern Dobruja between Varna and Cape Kaliakra and the ports of Varna and Kaliakra

ledger.note: 1356: Dobrotitsa's principality in Dobruja splits from the Second Bulgarian Empire. 'The Despotate of Dobruja existed from 1356 to 1411' (infobox 'Established: 1340s', Balik; Dobrotitsa from 1347 and 'despot' in 1357 on the Dobruja page); the pages give the region (between Varna and Cape Kaliakra), not a boundary.

region.text: Varna, Emona and Kozyak as the page names them

ledger.note: 1366: Varna, Emona and Kozyak pass to Dobrotitsa. After Amadeus of Savoy's fleet took Pomorie, Nessebar, Emona and Kozyak in autumn 1366 and was repulsed at Varna on 25 October, 'Varna, Emona and Kozyak were later ceded to Dobrotitsa'; the page does not date the cession, so 1366 is a bridge (the Bulgarian dossier also dates it 1366).

region.text: Pangalia (Mangalia) and other cities on the right bank of the Danube

ledger.note: 1368: the Danube-side cities recognise Dobrotitsa. 'Dobrotitsa was recognised as ruler by Pangalia and other cities on the right bank of the Danube.' The page does not say who held them before.

region.text: Anchialos (Pomorie) and Mesembria (Nessebar) on the Burgas coast

ledger.note: After 1369: Anchialos and Mesembria. The page says the despotate's control extended over 'some of the forts lost by the Bulgarians (Anchialos and Mesembria)' after 1369 and gives no year; 1375 is the year Cliopatria's shape adds the Nessebar cell. Pomorie and Nessebar were taken by Savoy in 1366 (Despotate page), so the Byzantine Empire as previous holder is the researcher's reading.
1386: Ivanko makes peace with Murad I and moves the capital from Kaliakra to Varna ('moved the capital from Kaliakra to Varna'; a commercial treaty with Genoa followed in 1387).

1388: the Ottomans overrun the Dobrujan forts. 'Ivanko was killed in 1388 during the expedition of Ottoman Grand Vizier Candarli Ali Pasha ... The expedition brought most of the Dobrujan forts under Turkish rule.' (The Despotate page tags the 1388 death 'citation needed' and the infobox puts Ivanko's reign to 1389.)
1388/1389: Dristra (Silistra) passes to Mircea the Elder. 'Dristra (Darstor) came under the control of Mircea the Elder' (the page dates it 1388/1389, citing a 1390 document).
1389: Varna falls to the Ottomans ('1389: Varna fell to the Ottomans'), the last seat of the Despotate.

region.text: what remained of Ivanko's Dobruja: the Black Sea coast from Varna to the Danube mouths

ledger.note: 1389: the Despotate ends with the fall of Varna. The Despotate page's lead says it 'existed from 1356 to 1411' and its Ivanko entry reads '1385-1389 and 1393-1399', but every dated event after 1389 on both pages is Ottoman or Wallachian (south 1393, Mircea 1395 and 1404, Ottomans 1397-1404 and 1420). Cliopatria ends it in 1394.

wars.name: Savoyard crusade (Amadeus of Savoy at Varna)

zones.text: Varna, Emona, Kozyak, Pomorie and Nessebar

wars.outcome: Amadeus's fleet took Pomorie, Nessebar, Emona and Kozyak in autumn 1366 and besieged Varna from 25 October without success; Varna, Emona and Kozyak were later ceded to Dobrotitsa.
wars.note: The page gives no year for the cession.

wars.name: Ottoman expedition against Dobruja (Candarli Ali Pasha)
wars.outcome: Ivanko killed in 1388; most of the Dobrujan forts under Ottoman rule; Varna fell in 1389.
wars.note: Death year 1388 per the Dobruja page; the Despotate page has it 'citation needed' and the infobox reign to 1389.

wars.name: Wallachian-Ottoman struggle for Dobruja

zones.text: Dobruja south of the Danube delta

wars.outcome: Mircea held Dristra from 1388/1389; Bayezid took the southern part in 1393; Mircea regained it in spring 1395; the Ottomans held it 1397-1404; Mircea imposed his authority in 1404; Mehmed I made the 'definitive conquest' in 1420.
wars.note: After the Despotate's end: kept so the land's later owners are on record.

certainty.note: Neither page gives a boundary or a treaty line; the limits are the Danube delta, the coast and the forts named (Varna, Kaliakra, Dristra).

sources.title: Despotate of Dobruja

sources.title: Dobruja
sources.note: Dobrotitsa's reign and territory, 1368 Pangalia, 1388 Ottoman expedition, Mircea the Elder 1388-1420, Ottoman annexation 1420.

notes: Pages: Despotate of Dobruja and Dobruja (budget 1-2). Settled: start 1356 (the Despotate page: 'existed from 1356 to 1411'; the Bulgarian dossier splits it in 1356; Cliopatria starts 1363). End: the dossier ends at 1389 (fall of Varna, ledger 1388-1389) although the Despotate page's lead says 1411 and Cliopatria draws it to 1394; the pages' own dated events after 1389 name Mircea and the Ottomans as holders, and the page's infobox rule list '1385-1389 and 1393-1399' for Ivanko is inconsistent with its own body (1388 death 'citation needed'). If the reviewer prefers the page's 1411, the 1390-1411 land would need a keyframe and the page is silent on its extent. Not settled: who held Anchialos and Mesembria in 1369-1375 (page: 'forts lost by the Bulgarians'); the date Emona and Kozyak were ceded; the Ottoman suzerainty (peace with Murad I in 1386; the page does not call it vassalage, so no vassal event). Counterparts: second-bulgarian-empire (eu-18-c records the 1356 split and the 1366 loss), ottoman-empire (me-10: gains 1388, 1389, 1393, 1397, 1420), principality-of-wallachia (Dristra 1388/89; Dobruja 1395, 1404-1420). Gazetteer: no new names (region Dobruja exists); capitals Kaliakra and Karvuna (Balchik) are not in places.jsonl.
